venue.name: Hatley Park Formal Gardens – National Historic Site
venue.description: Hatley Park is a National Historic Site and the campus of Royal Roads University, about 25 minutes from downtown Victoria, with an Edwardian castle, formal Italian, Japanese and rose gardens, forest trails and 565 oceanfront acres. Access to the formal gardens is free and they are open every day from 10 a.m. to dusk, entered through the garden booth beside Hatley Castle on College Drive. Hatley Castle is a working university building and its first floor can only be seen on a paid one-hour guided walking tour, which runs daily from May 8 to September 11. A small museum in the lower level of the castle holds two rooms of artifacts and panels on the Songhees and Esquimalt families, the Dunsmuir family and Royal Roads Military College.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The tours are wheelchair accessible. There are a number of accessible parking stalls located throughout the estate near the main entrances to each of the buildings.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Pay parking is in effect in all Royal Roads parking lots.

restrictions: Dogs must be on a leash at all times and are not permitted in the gated garden areas.
Access to Hatley Castle is only available with the guided tour.
Filming by drone is not permitted on the property.
venue.hours_notes: The gardens are open every day from 10 a.m. to dusk. Access to the formal gardens is through the garden booth beside Hatley Castle on College Drive. The Habitat Café, on the second floor of the Grant building, is open Monday to Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. and is closed on statutory holidays.
venue.seasonal_notes: Daily guided tours resume May 8 to September 11 (subject to change). The Hatley Castle museum is open to visitors from May to September (subject to change).
venue.price_year_or_season: Tour rates published for the May 8 to September 11 tour season; the page carries no year.

programs.name: Guided walking tour
programs.description: A one-hour guided walking tour taking in the first floor of Hatley Castle and the surrounding Italian Gardens, with guides covering the history of the Indigenous lands, the Dunsmuir family, Royal Roads Military College and Royal Roads University. Rates are plus GST: adult (18 to 59) $24.00, senior (60+) $20.00, youth (6 to 17 years) $15.00, child 5 and under free, and family (maximum 2 adults and 3 youth) $74.00. Tickets are sold in person only, at the Hatley Castle retail store inside the museum basement on the west side of the castle; they are not sold in advance, are first-come first-served subject to capacity, and sales close five minutes before each tour. Monday to Thursday there is an additional 4:15 p.m. departure on top of the four times recorded here.
programs.what_children_do: Walk for about an hour with a guide through the ground-floor rooms of a castle that is still a working university building, then out into the walled Italian Gardens, listening as the guide tells the history of the site.
programs.our_note: There is no advance booking and no group rate: tickets are sold at the counter on the day, first-come first-served, so a class arriving together may not all fit on the same tour. Under-sixes go free, but an hour on foot with no seating mentioned is long for that age. Ask how many places each tour holds before you commit a bus.
programs.practical_summary: The tour route is wheelchair accessible and there are accessible parking stalls across the estate. Washrooms, indoor lunch space, rain backup and bus parking are not stated on the site, so it is worth a call.
programs.extra_fees_note: Pay parking is in effect in all Royal Roads parking lots.
programs.payment_timing: Tickets are purchased in person at the Hatley Castle retail store before the tour and are not sold in advance.
programs.cancellation_note: Tour times are subject to change; the site asks visitors to check prior to visiting for cancellation updates and lists cancelled tour dates and times.

programs.name: Self-guided visit to the formal gardens
programs.description: Free access to the formal Italian, Japanese and rose gardens, entered through the garden booth beside Hatley Castle on College Drive. The gardens are open every day from 10 a.m. to dusk. Hatley Castle itself can only be entered on the guided tour, and dogs are not permitted inside the gated garden areas.
programs.what_children_do: Walk at their own pace through three walled gardens: the symmetrical Italian garden, the Japanese garden with its pond, walking bridge and water wheel, and the rose garden, and along the paths between them.
programs.our_note: This is the free option and needs no booking, but there is nothing indoors: the only shelter the site mentions is the café in the Grant building, which shuts at 2:30 p.m. and is closed on statutory holidays and weekends. Parking is pay parking in every campus lot, so budget for it. The gardens close early in bad weather. A wind closure notice was posted on the site the day before this check.
programs.practical_summary: Free, open daily from 10 a.m. to dusk, entered at the garden booth on College Drive. Washrooms, lunch space, rain backup, stroller access and bus parking are not stated on the site.
programs.extra_fees_note: Pay parking is in effect in all Royal Roads parking lots.
programs.evidence: The gardens are open every day from 10 a.m. to dusk.

programs.name: Hatley Castle museum visit
programs.description: The Hatley Castle museum, in the lower level of the castle, is open to visitors from May to September (subject to change). It holds two rooms. The Dunsmuir Room, with artifacts from James and Laura Dunsmuir's family life, and the Rear Admiral John A. Charles room, with Royal Roads Military College class photos, cadet uniforms, trophies and equipment, plus an entry hallway of panels introducing the Songhees and Esquimalt families and the early industrial development of the property. No separate admission price is published for the museum, and the same page's summary describes the museum visit as part of the guided walking estate tour, so it is unclear whether it can be entered on its own.
programs.what_children_do: Walk down a panelled hallway and through two rooms, looking at cadet uniforms, trophies, photographs, documents and Dunsmuir family objects in cases.
programs.our_note: Whether you can walk into the museum on its own or only with the paid tour is not clear from the site. The tour ticket desk is inside the museum basement, so ask at the counter when you arrive. Two rooms of cases and reading panels make for a short, quiet visit that suits school-age children rather than toddlers.
programs.practical_summary: Open May to September in the lower level of the castle. No admission price, opening hours, capacity or accessibility detail is published for the museum on its own.
programs.evidence: We welcome visitors to explore the Hatley Castle museum located in the lower level of Hatley Castle from May to September
